clusters.name: Absurd Silence, Searching Anyway
clusters.description: Protagonists adrift in an indifferent or surreal world, estranged from others and from meaning itself. Each confronts alienation, mortality, and moral responsibility, finding purpose only through action, solidarity, or the persistent search.

clusters.name: Tender, Tangled Twenties
clusters.description: Young adults fumbling toward intimacy, caught between desire, friendship, and self-protection. These books trace how love and close bonds shape, wound, and eventually help people grow into themselves.

clusters.name: Absurd Crises, Human Solidarity
clusters.description: Novels in which catastrophe or indifference strips away comforting illusions, exposing life's absurdity and society's fragility. They ask how individuals owe responsibility, compassion, and solidarity to one another when meaning is absent.

clusters.name: Living Through the Absurd
clusters.description: Philosophical novels that confront suffering, catastrophe, and political upheaval, questioning easy certainties about meaning, reason, and choice. Their characters find what dignity, solidarity, or love they can in a world that offers no guarantees.

clusters.name: Strangers in Ordinary Lives
clusters.description: Detached, estranged protagonists drift through mundane routines and social expectations, withdrawing or being pushed into strange inner and outer worlds. Each book probes alienation and the thin line between numb normalcy and the surreal.
